title: Throttlewise: adaptive batch calibrator with safe rollout
creator: Diego Ramos
description: Goal: build an adaptive batch calibration service ("Throttlewise") that continuously profiles serving workloads, proposes batching+cache parameter deltas, and applies them via a staged, observable rollout with automatic rollback triggers. The system should prioritize customer SLAs and cost savings, provide safe defaults, and produce reproducible simulations for proposed changes. This ticket covers design + PoC implementation of the calibrator, telemetry schema, and an operator-controlled safe apply flow.
acceptance_criteria: Profiler produces per-workload time-series of request interarrival, length distribution, and KV-hit ratios with max 5% overhead
Calibrator recommends batching window and target batch size with expected cost delta and 95th-latency delta estimate for each workload
Staged apply: canary (1%), ramp (10%,50%,100%) automation with health checks and automatic rollback if error rate + p95 latency regress > configured thresholds
Offline simulator reproduces 90% of estimated cost delta within +/-10% using historical traces
End-to-end telemetry surfaced in Console: per-workload recommendation, applied config, rollback events, and cost delta timeline

design_notes: Profiler: lightweight sample collector that tags by route, model, and customer. Store hourly histograms for seq_len, interarrival_ms, and kv_hit_ratio.

Heuristics: prefer batching where expected cost_saved_per_minute > epsilon and predicted p95_latency_impact < SLA_delta. Use conservative caps: max_batch_size <= 0.5 * current_peak_parallelism to avoid queuing storms.
Continuous tuning: run micro-experiments in background with randomized small offsets to parameters; accept only deltas that pass offline simulation and live canary checks.

Safe apply: canary -> ramp -> full with metrics observed at each step. Health metrics include p95 latency, error-rate, percent of requests hitting KV cache, and inferred queued_time. Rollback immediate if any metric breaches configured thresholds for >2 consecutive evaluation windows.
Simulator: deterministic replay of request traces against candidate batch sizes and cache policies; produce cost/latency estimate and confidence band.

Operator UX: Console card per-workload with recommended delta, estimated cost savings, expected risk band, and 'Apply (canary)' button. Enterprise customers can enable auto-apply after policy approval.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Automated batching could increase tail latency for latency-sensitive routes. Mitigation: route-level opt-out, conservative thresholds, and strict rollback triggers.
Risk: KV cache churn from aggressive cache policy changes. Mitigation: measure kv_hit_ratio, require a minimum baseline hit rate, and limit cache policy change frequency.
Risk: Measurement bias from sampling. Mitigation: validate sampler against full traces for a subset of customers and adjust sampling rate.
Risk: Interaction with autoscaling that masks queuing. Mitigation: synthetic load tests and tagging recommendations with expected pressure points.
